label: report test findings
_note: Draft written by the build; the team should review it against the QA module before a pilot.

items.question: List the parts of a good bug report, and say why the steps to reproduce matter most.
items.modelAnswer:
A short, specific title; the steps to reproduce; the expected result; the actual result; the environment (device, browser, version, test data); severity; and evidence such as a screenshot or log.

The steps matter most because a developer who cannot make the bug happen cannot confirm or fix it. Clear numbered steps turn "it doesn't work" into something anyone can repeat.

items.question: What is the difference between severity and priority? Give an example where they differ.
items.modelAnswer:
Severity is how badly the bug affects the system. Priority is how soon it should be fixed, which also depends on the business.

Example: the company name misspelt on the home page is low severity (nothing breaks) but high priority (every visitor sees it). A crash in a report run once a year can be high severity but lower priority.

items.question: At the end of a test cycle you write a short test summary for the team. What should it say?
items.modelAnswer:
What was tested and what was not; how many tests ran, passed, failed and were blocked; the open defects by severity, with the most serious named; any risks or known issues; and a clear recommendation, for example ready to release, or not ready until two critical bugs are fixed.

It should let a manager decide without reading every test case.
